requirements.md:237 (Non-goals, 'Scanning non-HTML files under specs/<feature>/mockups/') and requirements.md:248 (Edge Case 4) state a definite, security-relevant behavioral boundary: non-.html files (JSON fixtures, images, notes) placed under the scan target are never scanned, even if they contain a secret- or PII-shaped string. acceptance-tests.md's Test Matrix (lines 9-93) and Deferred section (95-103) contain zero rows asserting this exclusion (grep for 'non-HTML' and '*.html' across acceptance-tests.md returns no matches) -- contrast with TEST-002 (:12), which does positively test that nested .html files ARE detected, but no row tests the negative boundary that a non-.html file is NOT scanned/reported. Downstream failure mode: TEST-052's traceability manifest (:197) only checks AC-column coverage, not edge-case coverage, so this gap survives that check; an implementer could ship an overly broad file-selection glob (e.g. matching all files, or case-mismatched extensions) and pass every existing test while violating the documented product boundary, producing spurious blocks on non-HTML content with no acceptance test to catch the regression, and a task-decomposition reviewer has no row to decompose an implementation/verification task from for this boundary. This belongs to spec review because acceptance-tests.md is the Phase-1 traceability source tasks are built from (TEST-052), not an implementation-time defect. Major, not Critical, because no safety/workflow-boundary contradiction results and the fix is a single added test row.

The specification supplies enough concrete behavioral detail for a design reviewer to proceed without inventing product behavior: exit-code contract is exhaustive with precedence stated (requirements.md:47), named pattern-category identifiers are enumerated for design.md to fill in without re-deciding scope (AC-010:87-89, AC-011:91-93 name S1-S7/P1/P2 by role and rationale), masking is a stated security property not a design-invented one (AC-014:113-117), the override/decline/record-field contract is fully specified (REQ-006, AC-020-025), and cross-runtime parity requirements are explicit down to dual-form pattern expression (AC-038:99-101). The one gap found (EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE finding above) is a missing verification row for an already-stated behavior, not an undefined product decision, so it does not block handoff to implementation-policy review.
